$$
\frac{3-5\text{i}}{1+2\text{i}}
$$

The denominator is $1+2\text{i}$ and its conjugate is $1-2\text{i}.$ We multiply both the numerator and the denominator by $1-2\text{i},$ so that the denominator turns into a real number:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{{z}_{1}}{{z}_{2}} & =\frac{3-5\text{i}}{1+2\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{3-5\text{i}}{1+2\text{i}}\cdot \frac{1-2\text{i}}{1-2\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{3-6\text{i}-5\text{i}+10{\text{i}}^{2}}{{1}^{2}-{2}^{2}{\text{i}}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{3-11\text{i}+10(-1)}{{1}^{2}+{2}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{3-11\text{i}-10}{1+4} \\  & =\frac{-7-11\text{i}}{5}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form $a+b\text{i}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{-7-11\text{i}}{5}=-\frac{7}{5}-\frac{11}{5}\text{i}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
